method: Read all 8 frame PDFs (chain-3, 4, 5, 6, 6b, 7, 7b, 8). Drove Vite dev server at 127.0.0.1:5173 with Playwright (conda python, chromium, 1440x900). Captured every state in webui/smoke_pages/analyse.json for analyse.block and analyse.glyphs plus scrolled lower thirds, then probed ~30 interactions for dead clicks and dependent-panel updates. Zero console errors or page errors across all states.

pages.rationale: All seven frame templates (01 Baseline, 02 Noise floor, 03 Encoding, 04 Drop detection, Matrix profile, Threshold to spans, Model stage) are built to the frame's region hierarchy, proportions and copy, on the shared §6.5 shell (toolbar with source chip + back link + null chip + estimate + primary, clickable chain ribbon with signatures, process card, parameters, null, cost, hand-offs, footer). Empty/running/failed/missing and the live bridge mode are all present. Interactions are real and propagate: draggable cutlines and threshold, sweep click-to-set, try-other-windows, top-location re-centring, fix-merge, colour-by, card select, show-dropped, per-parameter info pop-overs, source-chip pop-over, SLURM job creation into Jobs with a toast, and hand-offs that navigate to Review/Interrogation/Models/Settings. Colour semantics, light plot ground, un-normalised mV, hours-since-start and the ≤10 detection cap all hold. Marked down from 9 for four data-consistency defects where a panel contradicts the page's own numbers or the frame's canon, and for a primary action clipped off the right edge at 1440.

findings.title: Primary action clipped off the right edge at 1440
findings.detail: After clicking 'Set merge window to 2.4 s' the toolbar grows (adds 'merge window 2 → 2.4 s · re-runs 04 → 04 ≈ 0.2 s') and the primary button overflows: measured getBoundingClientRect().right = 1460 on a 1440 viewport, so 'Apply & re-run from 04' renders as 'Apply & re-run from 0' with no way to scroll to it. The frames keep the toolbar on one line within the width. Same class of clipping appears at 1280 ('Re-run from…').

findings.title: 'What this change does downstream' is hard-coded and contradicts the page
findings.detail: Clicking 'Try other windows → 3 s' updates everything else correctly (plot redraws at 3 s, variance removed 59 %, residual drift 0.2 µV/s, red warning 'window 3 s < 2 × event length · this eats drop depth', card says 'depth kept 62 %'). But the downstream preview table stays byte-identical to the 7 s case: slope noise σ 0.0112 → 0.00958, raw detections 21 → 23, kept after dedupe 6 → 6, mean depth 0.27 → 0.31 mV. It claims a window that keeps 62 % of depth yields the same mean depth (0.31 mV) as the 7 s window. The panel is the frame's whole argument for this block, and it is the only one on the page that does not react.

findings.title: Encoding tiles contradict the null-sweep caption and drop the frame's canon values
findings.detail: At the default 8 σ the tiles read segments 250 · qualify as d 13 · qualify as u 8 · in SAME 81 %. The frame (chain-3) reads 250 · 23 · 31 · 60 %. The app still prints the frame's caption verbatim under the sweep — '8σ is the knee — the ratio jumps 2.7× → 7.7× while 23 d segments remain' — so the page says 23 and 13 for the same number on the same screen. Clicking the 4σ sweep bar gives tiles d 20 / u 24 while the sweep's own 4σ observed bar is ≈55 on a 'y: segments qualifying as d' axis, so tiles and sweep disagree at every value.

findings.title: Spans strip under the scores goes blank while the table still reports spans
findings.detail: At the recommended 2.5 σ the strip shows the span marks (5 <rect> nodes). Dragging the line to 3.35 σ leaves the strip empty — 1 <rect> in the DOM, nothing visible — while Output says 'spans 2', the table lists 2 rows ('1–2 of 2') and the hand-off reads 'Pass 2 to Review'. The strip is the page's answer to its own subtitle 'spans are what the next stage receives', so a blank strip beside a populated table is misleading. Everything else on the drag (cut slider, null cut line, spans-vs-cut line, Output, table, hand-off count) updates correctly.

findings.title: Failed state still presents a complete successful result
findings.detail: With state=failed the name chip reads '#134 failed', the ribbon badge is 'failed' and the banner reads '#134 failed here · ValueError: merge_window 2.0 s …', yet the page below is unchanged: '23 raw → 6 kept', the kept/surrogate/vs-chance tiles, six kept-detection cards M12–M17 and an enabled 'Pass 6 to Review'. Nothing marks the result as the last cached one. The chain-page copy for this run is 'No result · run #134 failed at 04 · nothing was written to detections'; §3 'nothing claims more than it knows' points the same way.

findings.title: Time axis reads 4-decimal hours where the frames read seconds
findings.detail: Frames chain-3/4/5/6 label the source chip '825–875 s' and the x axis '825 s … 875 s'. The app renders 'Signal span · CH4_A2 · 192.400–192.414 h' and ticks '192.4000 h · 192.4028 h · … · 192.4139 h'. Honouring the hours-since-start default is defensible, but four decimals over a 50 s span is far less legible than the frame's ticks, and 03 Encoding then mixes conventions in one card: 'showing 5–15 s of 50 s' above an axis in hours.

findings.title: Estimate chip reads 'last run run 14'; panel-1 exclusion-zone caption missing
findings.detail: Toolbar shows 'cached · last run run 14' (word doubled). Panel 1 carries 'query · m = 600 s' and 'nearest neighbour · d 2.4' but not the frame's middle caption 'grey · exclusion zone ± m/2', so the grey band behind the query is unexplained. The frame's toolbar estimate is '≈ 4 min · local'.

findings.title: Header subtitles truncated relative to the frames
findings.detail: Frame subtitles are 'show the process · judge the profile against its surrogate · then threshold', 'set the cut against the surrogate · spans are what the next stage receives', 'a registered model scores each window · its calibration becomes the next stage's recommended cut'. The app ships only the second clause, the first clause, and the first clause respectively. §3 calls these plain-language captions load-bearing.

findings.title: Control and chip text ellipsised where the frames show it in full
findings.detail: 'walk back from steepe…' (frame: 'walk back from steepest'), 'detected spans · iter…' (frame: 'detected spans · iterate 2×'), '3 motifs · 1 disco:' (frame: '3 motifs · 1 discord'), source chip collapsing to 'Signal span · CH4_…' whenever the estimate text grows. Two-column parameter cards are ~190 px narrower than the frame's.

findings.title: Run identity shows 'unsaved' instead of the canon run #128
findings.detail: Frame chain-4 names the run in the chip: 'drop_motifs9 ✎ run #128' and the estimate 'cached · last run 2 Sept', with the ribbon showing 04 cached. The app shows 'drop_motifs9 ✎ unsaved', 04 stale and 'retune ≈ 0.2 s · 03 → 04 recompute'. #128 drop_motifs9 is a §0 canon run.

findings.title: Derived readout and cutline values off by one digit from the spec
findings.detail: App: '8 σ puts ‘d’ at −0.0766 mV/s — faster than noise explains' and inner cutlines at ±0.029. §6.5 and frame chain-3: '−0.0767 mV/s' and cutlines U/D at ±0.028. The frame's wording is '— falling faster than the noise can explain'.

findings.title: Plot legend does not follow the view toggle
findings.detail: Switching stacked → difference redraws the panels as 'removed component (the baseline)' in orange and 'residual vs the recommended 7 s output' in purple, but the legend underneath still reads 'input · baseline · output · edge zone', naming series that are no longer on screen and omitting the two that are.

findings.title: Footer and header copy generic where the frame is specific
findings.detail: Frame: header '03 Noise floor', footer 'No unapplied changes · 02 is cached · changing σ here makes 03 and 04 stale', primary 'Re-run from 02'. App uses the generic template 'changing a parameter here makes 02 → 04 stale' and 'Re-run 02'. (The app's 02/03 numbering is in fact more self-consistent than the frame, which mislabels its own header.)

pages.rationale: A near-exact rebuild of frame chain-6b: title, both caption sentences, the six-entry colour key in the frame's order and hues, four group headers, and all 21 glyph cards in the frame's grouping and order, each with the 272×96 artwork, the 44×26 thumbnail and the full type signature in the DOM. It goes beyond the static frame with a working detail drawer (all three sizes side by side, registry name, category, null, used-by, Copy registry name, and 'Find it in Insert a stage' which really navigates to the chain's insert modal) and a filter with a proper empty state. No P0/P1: no dead clicks, no console errors, correct copy throughout. Held off 10 only by the signature ellipsis and a handful of glyph artworks that drift from the frame's drawing or its own colour key.

findings.title: Type signatures ellipsised on four cards
findings.detail: The card is too narrow for the longer signatures, so they render as 'Signal → Signal + est…', 'Signal + exemplar → S…', 'Model + WindowSet → S…', 'Encoding + labels → M…'. The full strings are in the DOM. The frame shows every signature complete, and §6.8 lists the type signature as a required part of what the glyph row carries.

findings.title: Gramian encoding glyph carries text labels the frame does not
findings.detail: The app draws the matrix plus a legend reading 'gasf' / 'gadf' with two swatches; at the 44×26 size that text is unreadable smudge. The frame's Gramian glyph is a plain blue/amber checkerboard with no lettering, and the page's own caption says glyphs are 'drawn once per algorithm, never from data' at a fixed 44×26 and 272×96.

findings.title: Three glyphs use hues the page's own colour key does not license
findings.detail: Surrogate generator adds a purple ✗ and two purple dots — purple is keyed 'exemplar / second input', and a surrogate generator has neither; the frame draws only a grey and a blue curve. Threshold to spans marks the found spans in blue where the frame uses green ('found / kept'). Hierarchical cluster draws its cut in amber where the frame uses red. Symbolic encoding and Window matrix each add a second row the frame's glyph does not have.

findings.title: Filter field is an addition the frame does not show
findings.detail: A 'filter glyphs' search box sits top-right of the title block; frame 6b has nothing there. It is required by the smoke manifest's filter-empty state and does no harm, but it is an extra control against the frame and slightly unbalances the header row.
